items.title: Ada Rovatti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 13, 2022
items.q: sometimes I put one of those Aebersold like C7 and the band plays C7.

ctx.x: Well you know it’s just with one chord of course it also depends also on the band you are playing with, it’s just like a blank, it’s a white canvas that you can just go in the direction you want. With one chord and then just like play out, in and out, and just kind of rhythmically — you study, there is a specific form with a specific rhythm and the chords change clearly you have some flexibility of reharmonization and playing in and out but you still have to kind of follow the chords and the form. So it’s a…

like I think it comes down to confidence and just bend the boundaries that we have in our inner ears. You know if you’re playing in C, and sometimes I put one of those Aebersold like C7 and the band plays C7. And I keep playing B7 or C#7 or F#7 and these totally out you know, clashing. But if you keep playing against those chords, you’re going to realize that your brain little by little easing up, It doesn’t hear that much, that dissonance. And as a matter of fact when you go back, in C, it sounds as if you’re…
Oh that’s wonderful. No one ever said that exactly like that.
